newsitem.title: UK: Physical Brent steady but Iraq keeps N.Sea quiet.
newsitem.headline: Physical Brent steady but Iraq keeps N.Sea quiet.

text.p: North Sea crudes were broadly steady in early Thursday trade as Dated Brent held but some grades showed signs of easing, traders said.
A Brent cargo due to load Aug 13-15 traded at Aug Brent +6 cents a barrel to a Wall Street trader, in line with the price fetched by an Aug 11-13 loader on Wednesday.
Traders said the North Sea market was divided over the prospect of an early resumption of Iraqi exports, with buyers and sellers equally relaxed.
"It's a very hard market to call at the moment," said one.
The U.N. is expected to complete its review of Baghdad's aid distribution plan this week, but some traders remained sceptical that Iraq had any intention of resuming exports quickly.
Nevertheless, shipping brokers reported U.S. trader Bayoil was seeking to fix Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) to take Iraqi crude oil from the port of Mina al-Bakr around the middle of August.
U.S. gasoline, which led a 38-cent jump in outright Brent levels on Wednesday, was stronger again in overnight ACCESS dealing but crude traders were nervous about following the market higher.
Sept Brent shed three cents on London's IPE to trade at $18.94 a barrel by 1234 GMT after hitting an eight-week high of $19.00 late on Wednesday.
Intermonth cash spreads were also barely moved with Aug/Sep talked at +12/+18 cents and Sep/Oct at -3/+1 cent, but Brent CFDs edged a shade higher.
Next week's Aug 4-8 dates were talked at Sept Brent +4/+8 cents, up from +2/+4 cents, with the following Aug 11-15 week gaining a couple of cents on the bid side.
No Brent cargoes were expected to be nominated loading dates on Thursday.

Other North Sea grades were beginning to feel the weight of unsold August cargoes. Two Oseberg cargoes traded at Dated Brent +23 cents and a third at +26 cents, down from previously talked levels around +30 cents.

Meanwhile, Statoil said it had adjusted the August loading programme for Statfjord crude oil due to unscheduled shutdowns at the Statfjord C and Snorre platforms and generally lower-than-forecast production at the field.
Traders said August liftings had been put back by three days and two of the originally scheduled 28 cargoes had been deferred to September.
